summary: One trade was approved: a TLT add, cut from $20 to $15. It filled at $81.698, above both earlier lots, and TLT closed at $81.49 (-0.38%). SPY's close-to-close move was about -0.49%, so TLT lost slightly less than stocks on the day and did not gain while they fell. One day says nothing about the hedge thesis. The account rose 0.63% to $615.73 against SPY's -0.49%. Since 11-10 it is -1.10%, against -2.88% for the shadow and -4.15% for SPY. Today's gain came from held names that the decision left alone: INCY +5.3%, KR +4.4% and IDXX +3.6%. close.json shows no stop_alerts and every stop block is ok. SAM is still the closest, 5.33% above $201. TLT is 6.8% above $76.30, DPZ 9.7% above its new $325 stop and IDXX 11.3% above $640. The reasoning holds up. The decision dealt with each of the Skeptic's points: it accepted the third-buy-in-four-sessions and averaging-up objection by resizing, and it rewrote TLT's sign-test clause as a relative test plus a trend test (L10), which was the clause objection. It also corrected the Proposer's wrong 'long-term-taxable' reason on DPZ and re-anchored DPZ's stop above the fill, since it cannot originate a trim. It cleared the stale SAM and IDXX text that L6 had flagged. It gave the Skeptic's low-confidence direction case little weight, which fits his 1-right, 17-wrong record and the Market Analyst's explicit duration call. Weak points: (1) The decision called today's Market Analyst note new evidence, but the 5-day figures (TLT +2.91%, SPY -2.39%) are the same week the 11-23 run had already counted. The $15 is a compromise between $10 and $20, not a size derived from a target weight. TLT has now been built in three tickets ($25, $10, $15) that each averaged up, and it is 8.1% of equity, the second-largest position, ahead of the 12-09 FOMC. (2) DPZ's new invalidation text says $325 is 'keeping most of the gain'. At the $356.52 close, a fall to $325 would keep only about $1.7 of the $8.2 unrealized gain. The level is reasonable, but the description is wrong, and it is the kind of stored text L6 says must be checkable. (3) Cash is about 50% (invested 50.4% against the shadow's 87.9%). The decision rightly named this as idled by the regime filter and not as a reason to keep any position. Because of that cash, the book's equity exposure is much lower than the owner's goal while SPY is under its 200-day. That is a design cost, not a decision error, but each added TLT dollar is a rates bet rather than a way to deploy cash toward the owner's diversification goal.
lessons: When re-anchoring a stop, describe it only by its distance from the fill or blended cost. Phrases like 'keeping most of the gain' depend on the mark and become false as it moves: DPZ's $325 keeps about $1.7 of an $8.2 gain at today's close. Fix DPZ's text at the next run: '$325, about 2.7% above the $316.58 fill'.

Restate TLT's stop at the next run from the actual blended cost after the 11-24 fill, about $81.10 across three lots ($80.75, $81.11, $81.698). $76.30 is about 5.9% under it (L6). The new relative clause (TLT's 5-day return below SPY's when SPY's 5-day is negative) is checkable from the next run's Market Analyst figures and should be stated there with values (L7).

When building a sleeve over several sessions on the same run of evidence, set a target weight for the sleeve once and size each add toward it. Don't re-split the difference between the Proposer's and the Skeptic's ticket each day. TLT reached 8.1% of equity in three averaging-up buys, and none of them stated where the sleeve should stop.

SAM's 11-19 8-K 5.02 ages out about 11-26 and is still unread, with SAM the holding nearest its stop. If the next run still cannot state Koch's continuing role, record it as closed by expiry and say so (L2). KR's 12-03 call enters the 5-day window on 11-25, so no KR adds from then on.
